Location: RETURNING TO THE BONFIRE › Resting at The Bonfire (manuscript.md line 1906)
Current text: Resting at the bonfire also revives lost characters who have been removed from play due to dying while hollow.
Proposed fix: A character who dies while hollow is lost. A lost character's model is placed on its side beside the bonfire tile and takes no further part in the encounter. When a character is lost, the encounter is failed immediately and the characters must rest at the bonfire. Resting at the bonfire revives all dead and lost characters.
Rationale: The term 'lost' appears at lines 1890, 1906 and 2235 but is never defined. Death & Hollowing (1223) already forces an immediate rest when a hollow character dies, so 'lost' is a transient state that must be named once and added to the glossary.
Gameplay impact: Players cannot tell whether a lost character differs from a dead one or whether lost characters return after a free (post-boss) rest.

Location: GAMEPLAY › Objective & Loss Conditions (manuscript.md line 1201); Death & Hollowing (line 1223)
Evidence: manuscript.md:1201, 1223, 1253, 1341; DS-Core-Rules-lores.txt p.8 ('Once the dial reads 0 ... the next time a character is killed, the game is lost')
Current text: The players lose collectively if at any point, all characters are dead and there are no remaining sparks to revive them.
Proposed fix: When the characters are forced to rest at the bonfire and the spark dial shows zero, the players lose the game. The characters may not choose to rest at the bonfire while the spark dial shows zero.
Rationale: A hollow character's death fails the encounter while other characters are still alive (1305); the forced rest then costs a spark that does not exist, and the stated loss condition (all characters dead) never triggers. The official rule ties the loss to a death at zero sparks; the manuscript's forced-rest model needs the equivalent.
Gameplay impact: The game's only end-state for defeat has no rule that applies in the commonest defeat sequence.

Location: GAMEPLAY › Souls (manuscript.md lines 1395–1399); Encounter Resolution (line 1331)
Current text: Dropped souls are lost forever if the character who dropped them dies before reclaiming the souls.
Proposed fix: Souls dropped by a character remain on the encounter tile where they were dropped. Souls dropped at the moment of death are not forfeited by that death; they are returned to the supply only if the same character dies again before reclaiming them. When an encounter is failed, every living character drops their souls on that tile in addition to any souls already there. A character reclaims their own dropped souls only by surviving to clear the encounter on the tile where the souls lie.
Rationale: A hollow character's death simultaneously drops souls (1207) and fails the encounter (1305), so the literal text ('dies before reclaiming') forfeits the souls dropped by that very death. Line 1331 also makes all characters drop souls, including characters whose souls already lie on the tile. Hollowed Edition keeps dropped souls until a second death.
Gameplay impact: Whether a hollow character's death wipes their souls is the single largest soul swing in the game and is currently ambiguous.

Location: GAMEPLAY › Death & Hollowing (manuscript.md line 1213)
Current text: If any character survives to clear an encounter, then the characters who died in that encounter are revived in a hollow state.
Proposed fix: A character adventuring alone never becomes hollow: when that character dies, the encounter is failed and the character must spend a spark to rest at the bonfire.
Rationale: The revival branch requires a surviving character; a solo death therefore always falls to the failed-encounter branch, which costs a spark. Stating this explicitly removes the question of whether a solo character ever hollows.
Gameplay impact: Solo players need to know that every death costs a spark (the official 1E outcome).

Location: GAMEPLAY › Death & Hollowing (manuscript.md line 1221) vs Resting at The Bonfire (line 1898), Boss Death (line 2195), PvP (line 3046)
Current text: Hollow status is only removed by using a spark or an ember token.
Proposed fix: Hollow status is removed only by resting at the bonfire or by becoming embered.
Rationale: Resting after a boss (2195) and before PvP (3046) costs no spark yet removes hollow cubes (1898). The restriction must name the rest, not the spark.
Gameplay impact: Literal reading leaves characters hollow after the free post-boss rest.

Location: GAMEPLAY › Embering (manuscript.md line 1229) vs CHARACTERS › Ember (line 805) and CHARACTER TURN › Major Action › Ember (line 1834)
Current text: Ember: Place ember token on dashboard; discard equipped ember card.
Proposed fix: Ember (major action, or at any time outside an encounter): Discard an ember card from the back-up slot. Remove all damage cubes and all hollow markers from the endurance bar and place an ember token on the dashboard. The character is now embered.
Rationale: Three passages define embering; only Embering (1229) says it removes all damage cubes. A full heal as a major action is a major tactical resource and must be stated identically everywhere. Alternative: delete 'Remove all damage cubes' at 1229 so that embering only removes hollow markers (Hollowed Edition precedent, p.5).
Gameplay impact: Groups will disagree on whether embering heals; the difference is up to eight health in combat.

Location: GAMEPLAY › Embering (manuscript.md line 1243); Shop Rules (line 1949); Boss Death (line 2195)
Current text: Characters cannot carry an ember card while embered.
Proposed fix: When a character becomes embered while holding an ember card, that character must immediately give the ember card to another character who is neither embered nor holding an ember card. If no such character exists, the ember card is returned to the tier one shop.
Rationale: Boss Death embers every character at once (2195), so a character holding an ember card is placed in an illegal state with no resolution. Alternative: return the card to the game box.
Gameplay impact: Rare but guaranteed to arise after the first boss when a character has bought an ember.

Location: GAMEPLAY › Encounters › Encounter Start step 2 (manuscript.md lines 1261–1263) vs CHARACTERS › Endurance Bar (line 787)
Current text: A character may never elect to spend excess stamina at the cost of receiving a staggered condition marker.
Proposed fix: The characters may skip cleared encounters only if every character can place all of the required stamina cubes without exceeding their endurance bar. A hollow character has six spaces. The stamina cubes for skipped encounters are placed at the start of the next encounter the characters fight.
Rationale: Skipping is elective, costs two stamina per skipped encounter per character, and a hollow character has six spaces; skipping four encounters (eight stamina) is therefore impossible under line 787, yet campaign sections list up to five encounters. Alternative: allow the skip and place a single stagger token for the overflow.
Gameplay impact: Determines whether hollow characters can use the skip mechanic at all in long sections.

Location: CHARACTERS › Endurance Bar (manuscript.md line 787); Conditions › Stagger (line 1634)
Current text: Stagger tokens are limited to one per model.
Proposed fix: If a character who is already staggered is forced to place a stamina cube when no space remains, the cube is not placed and no further effect occurs.
Rationale: Stamina overflow converts to a stagger token, and stagger is capped at one; the second overflow has no stated outcome.
Gameplay impact: Edge case only; prevents table arguments about repeated overflow.

Location: COMBAT BASICS › Conditions › Frostbite (manuscript.md line 1626) vs CHARACTER TURN › Recover one stamina (line 1802), Rest (line 1826), Encounter Recovery (lines 1349–1351)

Rationale: The mandatory 'Recover one stamina' step and the Rest action are both stamina recovery; the text must say that both are blocked. Encounter Recovery lists stamina removal before condition removal, so a frostbitten survivor is blocked from the end-of-encounter recovery by the literal order.
Gameplay impact: Clarifies a condition that otherwise silently disables a whole turn step.

Location: CHARACTER TURN › Major Action › Rest (manuscript.md line 1826)
Current text: Rest: Restore all of the character's stamina, if no run action was taken this turn.
Proposed fix: Rest: Remove all stamina cubes from the endurance bar. A character who rests may not run during the same turn, before or after resting. Walk, Equip and Heroic Action remain available.
Rationale: The condition 'taken this turn' only forbids running before the Rest; a character resting first and then running to full stamina would exploit the ordering.
Gameplay impact: Prevents a free full-stamina sprint every other turn.

Location: CHARACTERS › Character Tokens (manuscript.md line 793) — Estus Flask absent from body; DOCX footer only

Location: GAMEPLAY › Encounters › Encounter Turn Order step 3 (manuscript.md line 1291); ENEMY TURN › Enemy Movement (line 1672)
Evidence: manuscript.md:1275, 1291–1293, 1672, 1682; DS-Core-Rules-lores.txt p.22 (aggro passes on activation)
Current text: After all characters have taken their turn, place the aggro token on the character who placed the most damage tokens on enemy models.
Proposed fix: When the character holding the aggro token dies, immediately place the aggro token on the living character with the highest threat value; if several are tied, the players choose. The aggro token is never held by a dead character.
Rationale: Enemy movement and attacks target the aggro holder; nothing says what happens when that character is removed from play mid-round. In the official game the token moves every character activation, so the state never arises.
Gameplay impact: Enemy behaviours become unresolvable for the rest of the round after a death.

Location: SETUP › Character Setup step 7 (manuscript.md line 1001); Encounter Start step 8 (line 1275); Encounter Turn Order step 2 (line 1289)
Current text: Each character takes their turn one-by-one in descending threat value.
Proposed fix: If two or more characters share a threat value, the players choose which of them receives the aggro token and the order in which the tied characters take their turns.
Rationale: Several character dashboards share threat values; no tie-break is given for either the aggro assignment or the turn order.
Gameplay impact: Common with two characters of the same class family; cheap to fix.

Location: GAMEPLAY › Encounters › Encounter Turn Order step 3 (manuscript.md line 1291)
Current text: ...the character who placed the most damage tokens on enemy models.
Proposed fix: After all characters have taken their turns, place the aggro token on the character who inflicted the most damage on enemy models during that round, counting damage recorded on an invader's or boss's health dial as well as damage tokens.
Rationale: Invaders track damage on a dial, not with tokens; the literal measure excludes damage to invaders. The phrase 'that round' is also needed so that cumulative damage is not counted.
Gameplay impact: Prevents the aggro token ignoring the character fighting the invader.

Location: SUMMONS › Phantoms (manuscript.md lines 1971–1993)
Evidence: manuscript.md:1971–1993; DS-Phantoms-Rules-lores.txt p.6 (summons have taunt levels and block/resist/dodge values like characters), p.8–9 (weak-arc die, Distract icon, deck renewal)
Current text: Phantoms take their turn after all character turns are resolved and before the first enemy turn begins.
Proposed fix: A phantom is treated as a character for enemy targeting, range and node limits. A phantom never holds the aggro token unless a Distract icon on its behaviour card is resolved, in which case the phantom is treated as holding the aggro token until the end of the next boss turn. A phantom defends with the block, resist and dodge values on its data card, rolling dice as a character does. A phantom's health is not scaled. Phantoms gain the weak-arc black die. When a phantom's behaviour deck is empty, flip its discard pile face-down without shuffling.
Rationale: The manuscript gives a summoning procedure but none of the rules the Phantoms booklet supplies for how a summon is targeted, defends, interacts with aggro or renews its deck. A phantom with a health dial (1993) must be attackable, so targeting must be defined.
Gameplay impact: Boss behaviours cannot be resolved when a phantom is nearest or holds no defined aggro status.

Location: GAMEPLAY › Encounters › Encounter Start step 9 (manuscript.md line 1277); PLAYER VS PLAYER (line 3056)

Rationale: The first player token is not in the component list and is never used: character order is fixed by threat value (1289), so the token has no function. PvP calls the same object a 'First turn token'.
Gameplay impact: Removes a phantom component and a contradiction between two names.

Location: BOSS TURNS › Boss Aggro (manuscript.md line 2191); Parry & Riposte (line 1790)
Current text: ...simply move the aggro token to a character's dashboard if they deal any damage to the boss during their turn.

Rationale: A riposte is an out-of-turn attack; the boss aggro rule only covers damage dealt 'during their turn'.
Gameplay impact: Edge case created by the manuscript's own parry rule.

Location: BOSS TURNS › Boss Turn Overview (manuscript.md line 2157)
Current text: characters must take an equal number of turns and cannot take a turn until every other character has taken an equal number of turns.
Proposed fix: Dead characters are ignored when counting turns. Within each round the living characters choose the order in which they take their turns, and no living character takes a second turn in a round until every other living character has taken one.
Rationale: A dead character can take no turns, so the literal equal-turns rule blocks every living character once anyone dies in a boss fight.
Gameplay impact: Boss fights after a death become unplayable as written.

Location: SUMMONS › Phantoms step 6 (manuscript.md line 1987) vs BOSS TURNS › Boss Turn Overview (line 2157)
Evidence: manuscript.md:1971, 1987, 2157; DS-Phantoms-Rules-lores.txt p.8 (summon activates after each character activation)
Current text: Phantoms take their turn after all character turns are resolved and before the first enemy turn begins.
Proposed fix: In a boss encounter the phantom takes its turn after each character turn and before the following boss turn.
Rationale: Phantoms are only ever summoned into boss encounters (1971), where boss and character turns alternate one at a time; 'after all character turns' has no meaning in that structure. The official rule is one phantom turn per character turn. Alternative: one phantom turn per full round of character turns.
Gameplay impact: Phantom activation frequency changes its value by a factor of up to four.

Location: SUMMONS › Invaders › Invader Tokens (manuscript.md lines 2007–2011)
Current text: Place an invader token face-down on each face-down encounter card.
Proposed fix: Invaders never appear in boss encounters or mimic encounters.
Rationale: Boss tiles carry no encounter card, so the exclusion follows from the placement rule but is never stated; the invader-after-each-character turn rule (2025) would otherwise be read against the boss alternation.
Gameplay impact: Removes a question every group asks when the invader token is still unrevealed at the fog gate.

Location: BOSS TURNS › Boss Turn Overview (manuscript.md line 2157) vs Encounter Turn Order step 2 (line 1289)
Current text: After each boss turn, one character may take their turn, then the boss takes another turn, a second character, and so-on.
Proposed fix: In boss encounters the players choose which living character takes each character turn, subject to the equal-turns rule. The descending threat order of ordinary encounters does not apply.
Rationale: Ordinary encounters fix character order by threat (1289); boss encounters say 'one character may take their turn', which implies free choice without saying so. Alternative: apply threat order in boss encounters as well.
Gameplay impact: Determines whether players can sequence the healer after the tank in boss fights.

Location: ENEMY TURN › Enemy Attacks (manuscript.md line 1706)
Evidence: manuscript.md:1672, 1706, 1596; DS-Core-Rules-lores.txt p.25 (attack target icons, node icon, out-of-range miss, movement attacks); DS-TG-Rulebook p.25
Current text: Additional symbols beside the attack type icon modify the attack with special rules detailed later.
Proposed fix: An enemy attack targets the character shown by the small icon beside the attack icon: the skull icon targets the character with the aggro token; the ring icon targets the nearest character, with ties resolved as for enemy movement. If the target is not within the attack's range, the attack misses and has no effect. An attack with the node icon targets every character on the target's node; each targeted character defends separately. A push-movement that shows a damage value is a physical attack against every character on each node the enemy moves into, resolved separately for each character and defended as a normal attack.
Rationale: The promised 'special rules detailed later' never appear. Target selection, node (area) attacks and the out-of-range miss are defined only for movement, and the manuscript's push-movement paragraph (1594) never says that the damage number is an attack. Every enemy data card depends on these icons.
Gameplay impact: Enemy attacks cannot be resolved from the manuscript alone.

Location: COMBAT BASICS › Enemy Scaling (manuscript.md line 1529); Character Attacks › Repeat (line 1872); Boss Attacks (line 2187)
Evidence: manuscript.md:1529, 1579, 1872, 2187; DS-Core-Rules-lores.txt p.40 ('Repeat behaviour or attack' icon exists on official cards)
Current text: If playing with four characters, add repeat to each non-boss enemy's attack behaviour.
Proposed fix: When Repeat 2 is added by scaling, each attack icon on the enemy's data card is resolved twice in succession against the same target before the next icon is resolved. The damage value of a push-movement is not an attack icon and is not repeated. If an attack icon already bears a Repeat icon, increase its value by one.
Rationale: Repeat is defined for weapons (entire option) and bosses (entire card) but not for non-boss enemies, and official data cards already carry Repeat icons. Alternative: Repeat added by scaling does not stack with a printed Repeat icon.
Gameplay impact: Four-player games double or quadruple some enemy damage output depending on the reading.

Location: COMBAT BASICS › Enemy Scaling (manuscript.md line 1527); CAMPAIGN PLAY › Bonfire Ascetic (line 2342)
Current text: If playing with three or more characters, increase all non-boss attack values by one.
Proposed fix: Attack value increases from scaling and from the bonfire ascetic apply to every attack icon and to the damage value of push-movements.
Rationale: Push-movement damage (1702) is a number inside a movement icon, not an 'attack value'; the scaling text does not say whether it is increased. Alternative: push-movement damage is never modified.
Gameplay impact: Trampling enemies (Sentinel, Smelter-type) are the ones where the +1 matters most.

Location: COMBAT BASICS › Enemy Data Cards (manuscript.md line 1517) vs Enemy Scaling (line 1523 and table at 1533–1584)
Current text: When playing with more than one character, calculate a scaled health value by adding one health for each character (including dead characters) in play.
Proposed fix: When playing with more than one character, add one health for each character in play beyond the first (including dead characters).
Rationale: Literal reading of 1517 gives Base+2 for two characters; the table and line 1523 give Base+1.
Gameplay impact: Off-by-one on every enemy's health in multiplayer.

Location: CAMPAIGN PLAY › Adding & Dropping Players (manuscript.md line 2239) vs Enemy Scaling (line 1523)
Current text: If a player character leaves the characters, the characters gain one spark, the character's equipment is added to the inventory, and the maximum number of sparks is changed...
Proposed fix: A character who has left the campaign is not counted for enemy scaling, per-character rewards, shop ember cards or the spark maximum from the moment the player leaves. A new character is counted from the moment the player joins.
Rationale: Scaling counts 'dead characters' but nothing addresses departed ones; per-character treasure already dealt to tiles also changes count.
Gameplay impact: Prevents a dropped player inflating enemy health for the rest of the section.

Location: SUMMONS › Invader Encounter Setup step 3 (manuscript.md line 2019); CRYSTAL LIZARDS (line 2055); Enemy Scaling (line 1521)

The bonfire ascetic (2342) already exempts invaders from +1 attack, which shows the intent. Alternative: invaders receive attack scaling but not health scaling.

Location: GAMEPLAY › Objective & Loss Conditions (manuscript.md line 1201) vs PLAYER VS PLAYER (line 3042)
Current text: Players may also choose to add a player versus player (PvP) encounter after the final boss is defeated ... / After each boss (mini, main, and mega) a PvP encounter will occur.
Proposed fix: If the players chose PvP during setup, a PvP encounter is played after each boss encounter (mini, main and mega) is cleared and before the characters rest at the bonfire.
Rationale: The objective text says PvP happens once, after the final boss; the PvP chapter says after every boss and its '+1 attack damage in future PvP' rule only makes sense with several PvP rounds. Alternative: a single PvP encounter after the final boss and deletion of the +1 rule.
Gameplay impact: Decides how many PvP rounds a game contains.

Location: PLAYER VS PLAYER (manuscript.md lines 3040–3094)
Current text: Character turn structure is unchanged from basic rules. ... Dodge difficulty is based on an the attacker attack option's stamina cost
Proposed fix: When a character attacks another character, the attacker resolves the attack option as if against an enemy and determines the final attack value. The defender then chooses to block, resist, dodge or parry exactly as against an enemy attack whose attack value equals that final attack value and whose dodge difficulty is given by the stamina-cost table. Damage suffered equals the attack value minus the defence total. Push, condition, shift and area-of-effect icons apply to characters as they apply to enemies; an area-of-effect attack targets every other character on the target node. A parry requires the attacker to share the defender's node; a successful parry staggers the attacker and permits a riposte. Block and resist values of defenders are never subtracted from the attack value; defence is always rolled.
Rationale: The PvP chapter supplies turn order, traps and a dodge table but never says how a character-versus-character attack is resolved: the enemy-attack procedure assumes a fixed attack value, the character-attack procedure assumes a fixed block value, and neither covers push, AoE, conditions or parry against a character.
Gameplay impact: PvP cannot be played from the text.

Location: PLAYER VS PLAYER (manuscript.md lines 3062–3066)
Evidence: manuscript.md:713, 967–981, 3062–3066; DS-Core-Rules-lores.txt p.18 (trap tokens show a dodge value and damage, or are blank)
Current text: Players place a trap token on an outermost available node after each turn. Characters that move onto a trap token may attempt to dodge. Characters that fail to dodge a trap immediately die.
Proposed fix: After each character turn, the player who took that turn draws a random trap token from the supply and places it face-up on an unoccupied outermost node (a node touching the tile edge) that holds no terrain or trap token; if no such node exists, the token is placed on any unoccupied node. A character who moves onto or is pushed onto a trap token rolls dodge dice against the trap's dodge difficulty; a blank token has no effect and is removed. On a failed dodge the character dies.
Rationale: Which player places the token, which token, whether it is face-up, what 'available' and 'outermost' mean, and how a trap's dodge difficulty is read are all unstated. The arena-shrinking effect is the only mechanism that ends a ranged stalemate, so it must work.
Gameplay impact: Without this the PvP end condition can never be reached between two cautious players.

Location: PLAYER VS PLAYER (manuscript.md lines 3050, 3076–3078)
Current text: Dead characters are excluded from PvP. ... Victory on non-final bosses provides +1 attack damage in future PvP only.
Proposed fix: The PvP encounter is played after dead characters have been revived and every character has been restored as if rested. A PvP encounter with fewer than two living characters is not played. Record a PvP victory by placing a 1-soul token from the supply on the champion's dashboard; in later PvP encounters the champion adds one to the attack value of every attack against a character.
Rationale: Clearing a boss revives the dead as hollow (1213) and PvP restores everyone (3046), so 'dead characters are excluded' is unreachable; and no marker is defined for the +1 bonus.
Gameplay impact: Removes an unreachable rule and gives the bonus a physical tracker.

Location: PLAYER VS PLAYER (manuscript.md line 3076)
Current text: The last character alive is awarded victory.
Proposed fix: If three consecutive rounds pass in which no character suffers damage, every character suffers one damage at the end of each further round until the encounter ends.
Rationale: Two ranged characters can retreat indefinitely; traps shrink the arena only slowly and a player may choose placements that never threaten themself. Alternative: rely on trap placement alone.
Gameplay impact: Guarantees termination of the optional mode.

Location: BOSS ENCOUNTERS › Character Arc Movement (manuscript.md line 2143)
Evidence: manuscript.md:2143; DS-Core-Rules-lores.txt p.28; Dark_Souls_The_Board_Game_FAQ.txt (push by boss attack: any node farther from attacker)
Current text: If the character is pushed off of the boss's node, they must move to the centre-most node in the boss's arc they originate from, if possible.
Proposed fix: If a character is pushed off a boss's node, the character moves to a node adjacent to the boss's node within the same arc, chosen by the players. If no such node exists because of a wall or terrain, the character moves to any adjacent node touching that wall.
Rationale: 'Centre-most node' is undefined (arcs are wedges with no centre node on most tiles). The manuscript deliberately keeps the same-arc rule for pushes, which the FAQ relaxed; the simpler wording keeps that choice. Alternative: adopt the FAQ ruling (any adjacent node farther from the boss).
Gameplay impact: Frequent event in every boss fight.

Location: BOSS ENCOUNTERS › Attacking Bosses and Weak Arcs (manuscript.md line 2149)
Current text: If the character is attacking a weak arc, the attack gains an additional black die.
Proposed fix: The additional black die is rolled for each attack roll made against a weak arc, including each repetition of a Repeat attack and each riposte.
Rationale: A Repeat option is 'that entire weapon option' used several times; whether each roll gains the die is unstated.
Gameplay impact: Small but constant in boss fights with Repeat weapons.

Location: BOSS TURNS › Boss Movement & Symbols (manuscript.md line 2175)
Current text: If a boss leaps into a node occupied by a character, the boss maintains its original facing and the character(s) are pushed into any adjacent node of their choosing unrestricted by the boss arc.
Proposed fix: Leap: Remove the boss from the tile and place it on the node of its target, the character with the aggro token or the nearest character as shown on the icon. A leap has no distance limit. The boss keeps its facing. Every character on that node is pushed to an adjacent node of that character's choice and is not placed in any arc.
Rationale: The Turn and Rotate icons are defined but the Leap icon that the sentence depends on is not, and nothing says the leap targets a character.
Gameplay impact: Leap appears on core mini-boss and main-boss cards; unresolvable without a definition.

Location: GAME COMPONENTS › Main-Bosses (manuscript.md lines 509–511) vs CAMPAIGNS (lines 2398, 2500, 2660, 2934); Node Model Limits (line 921)
Evidence: manuscript.md:509, 511, 921, 2157, 2191, 2398; DS-Core-Rules-lores.txt p.5 ('Dragon Slayer Ornstein & Executioner Smough' is one main boss), p.21
Current text: Dragon Slayer Ornstein (Core) / Executioner Smough (Core) ... Ornstein & Smough (main-boss)
